FIELD REPORT: ON CERYS SABLEWOOD THE ASHEN

Filed by: an ash-road observer Subject: Cerys Sablewood the Ashen
Condition of testimony: incomplete; certain passages rest upon
overheard speech and may be colored by fear

Cerys Sablewood the Ashen is a major Master of Coin. This much is
repeated wherever coin is counted, weighed, hidden, or denied.
Whether the title is borne by right, purchase, or necessity, I
cannot establish. Cerys was born in 330 AS, though the date is
spoken more confidently by ledgers than by living mouths.

The subject presents the controlled, calculating atmosphere expected
of a Master of Coin carrying a hidden royal inheritance. I record
the wording carefully: Cerys is the unacknowledged heir to the
Bleeding Crown. “Unacknowledged” is the hinge upon which all other
statements turn. The claim is not openly owned, yet it follows Cerys
like smoke beneath a door. Some who speak of it lower their voices.
Others smile as though they have discovered a profitable joke. I
advise neither practice.

No canonical physical features are established for Cerys Sablewood
the Ashen. Reports that offer height, coloring, scars, or other
bodily particulars are therefore unverified and should not be
entered into a serious account. The epithet “the Ashen” provides
Cerys’s defining visual identity. It is less an ornament than a
shadow placed upon the name. Those who insist they saw some
unmistakable sign may be remembering the title rather than the
person.

In dealings, Cerys is said to make silence feel like an assessment.
A pause becomes a measure. A glance becomes an inventory. Even an
empty purse seems, in Cerys’s presence, to possess a hidden
compartment. I cannot say whether this is craft or merely the effect
of expecting craft. The difference matters to scholars and not at
all to those awaiting an answer.

No testimony gathered here proves that Cerys openly claims the
Bleeding Crown. No testimony proves that the Crown accepts Cerys.
The inheritance remains hidden and unacknowledged, which may be the
same as powerless, or may be the exact condition required for power
to survive.

Final assessment: treat Cerys Sablewood the Ashen as a major Master

of Coin, born in 330 AS, and as the unacknowledged heir to the
Bleeding Crown. Treat every further certainty as a coin held up to
the light: possibly genuine, possibly shaved, and never offered
without purpose.
